catalog_quote: 1.6.1. Tone plays a very important role in Hmar With the change of tone, same word may mean two different things. ... 1.6.2. Three distinct tones could be identified for Hmar. They are — i) Level tone which indicates that the constituent sounds of the word are pronounced at the same pitch as in the normal speech in a non-tonal language, and this is unmarked. ii) Raising tone which suggests that the pitch over the pronunciation of a vowel suddenly rises from that of the level tone ... iii) Falling tone which suggests that there is sudden fall of the pitch over the pronunciation of a vowel from that of the level tone ... All the three tones may be present in initial, medial or final positions in the words spoken. ... Marking of the tone is necessary when words occur in sentences. In isolation words may occur in level tone only. ... 1.6.5. The tone of a word in a sentence may differ from t…

sources.citation: Infimate, Marina L. 2023. Causativization in Hmar. Himalayan Linguistics 22(1): 142-165. doi:10.5070/H921255411
sources.quote: 'Hmar is a tonal language and follows SOV as its basic word order.' Footnote 3: 'It must be noted that a full tonal analysis in Hmar has not been carried out yet. As such, the system of marking tone in the paper is to be considered provisional.' No mention of word stress anywhere in the paper (grep of full text: 'stress' absent).
